@jiajliu: This pull request explicitly references no jira issue.

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-version-operator/pull/1336):

>Added a "Migrating from Custom Tags" section for migrating tests from openshift-tests-private to align with upstream test label conventions.
>
>- Custom tag mapping table: Documents how to handle tags like `NonPreRelease`, `Longduration`, `ConnectedOnly`, `NonHyperShiftHOST`, etc.
>- Runtime skip guidance: Instructions for implementing programmatic skips for infrastructure/topology constraints
>- Custom test suites: Examples for using Ginkgo labels and CEL qualifiers to organize tests when standard test suites don't meet specific needs
>
>This ensures consistent migration practices and prevents CI breakages during test migration.

/lgtm  but small suggestion related to author or case ID, if we can add custom label for Case ID and author it will be easy to track the failures in future.

> /lgtm but small suggestion related to author or case ID, if we can add custom label for Case ID and author it will be easy to track the failures in future.

To align with the practices for developer-contributed cases in this repository, custom fields from OTP such as "author" and "case ID" are not mandatory labels during OTP/OTE migration.

You've raised a good concern regarding failure tracking. AFAIK custom labels are not displayed alongside the case name in the CI results. For example: the [case with custom label](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-version-operator/blob/main/test/cvo/cvo.go#L60C8-L60C36) like `g.It("should have a network policy", g.Label("OCPBUGS-77762")` while there is only name `: [Jira:"Cluster Version Operator"] cluster-version-operator should have a network policy` shown in [CI test result](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/pr-logs/pull/openshift_cluster-version-operator/1347/pull-ci-openshift-cluster-version-operator-main-e2e-agnostic-ovn/2032344270085558272). That means we still have to check the code to understand the specific characteristics of a failed case.

For short-term, authors optionally can use [comments](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-version-operator/blob/main/test/cvo/cvo.go#L74) or [custom labels](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-version-operator/blob/main/test/cvo/cvo.go#L60) for case identification. For long-term, we might further discuss a team-wide unified approach among the team and then update the readme file together.

This is a doc update and does not require testing.
